- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast 3–5 days ahead, averaging last 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underperform; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–7 days.
